title: Maximum Frequency of an Element After Performing Operations I
summary: Given an integer array nums, integers k and numOperations, perform numOperations operations where each operation involves selecting an unselected index and adding a value in the range [-k, k] to the element at that index.
statement: Given an integer array nums, integers k and numOperations, perform numOperations operations where each operation involves selecting an unselected index and adding a value in the range [-k, k] to the element at that index. The goal is to determine the highest frequency any element in nums can achieve after all operations.
constraints: nums has 1–100,000 values in 1..100,000; k is nonnegative and num_operations is at most len(nums).
Each selected index may change once by any integer in [-k,k], including zero.
Return the largest achievable frequency after exactly num_operations selections.
hints: A value x can reach every integer target in the interval [x-k,x+k].
Sweep interval events while separately counting values already equal to each candidate target.
At each event coordinate, cap reachable values by existing[target]+available operations.
The sweep gives every target’s convertible population, and only nonmatching members of that population require operations.
editorial: The sweep gives every target’s convertible population, and only nonmatching members of that population require operations.

tests.explanation: Changing five to four yields frequency two; the other required selection may add zero.
The existing pair of twenties already gives frequency two, and the operation may add zero elsewhere.
